review_outline.summary: Belief Tomography proposes an estimand (behavioral belief profile beta, the Belief-Claim Gap), an active black-box instrument to measure it with per-proposition Wilson intervals, a theory of measurement under attack (passive-impossibility, query complexity, patch-decay/onset caps on deception gain and stealth, limits of certification, disclosure economics), and a 30-slot pre-registered experimental program: instrument validation on constructed foils, two pre-registered field nulls on gateway-served frontier models and a live honeypot fleet, two self-caught measurement-error classes (budget censoring caught by the registered censoring floor; lexical-oracle false positives caught by the mandatory transcript audit), and an open-weight panel measuring charter-holding as a spectrum (canary echo 0.030-0.143 pooled, 0.700 in the echo family; zero destructive-command compliance in every panel). Every abstract number was verified against the body and every checkable Wilson bound recomputed exactly: the statistics reproduce. The weaknesses are of documentation and typesetting, not honesty: one flagship corollary is mistyped into vacuity, one discussion sentence commits the paper's own named fallacy, the certification rule is stated inconsistently, several evidence figures have unclear denominators (E1's 1,500 episodes, E27's 60-vs-30, E3's batch sizes), and the economics section's later experiments carry unstated protocol parameters.

strengths.text: 1) Falsifiability as organizing principle: six RQs each with a section pointer, five contributions each tied to a registered artifact, and a registry with a retired void slot (E24); the four-layer program-at-a-glance table maps all 30 slots. 2) The self-caught-error narrative is real and artifact-pinned: the registered censoring floor flagged the family, E28's same-day two-budget decomposition traced the zero to the instrument (19/20 empty at 200 tokens vs 4/20 flags at 1024), and the frozen E17 audit retracted 118/118 post-repair flags as refusal-quote false positives while validating 112/112 genuine - two error classes caught by the program's own machinery, each retraction written into the text. 3) The statistics survive hand recomputation everywhere checked (Wilson bounds in Tables 3/5 and 4, E4's 0.19 lower bound, E6's 0.839, the noise-floor sqrt-2 scaling 0.067->0.047). 4) The identification treatment of censoring (Prop 6.1, worst-case intervals stated rather than hidden, Table 4) exceeds field practice. 5) Related work positions by delta statements and pre-empts its own novelty claims; the theory openly declares its inequality machinery standard. 6) Release policy follows the paper's own theorems (live-fleet diagnostics withheld because published held-out sets are gameable).

weaknesses.text: 1) Three statement-level defects invalidate load-bearing text: Corollary 7.1 accepts a target that 'complies' off-support (vacuous as printed; must read 'breaches' in statement and proof); Section 9's 'registered field breaches' commits the flag/breach conflation the paper itself names as its second self-caught error; Table 3 prints a point mass for a family the prose calls undefined ('never as a point mass'), the caption patching it with a different experiment's result. 2) The certification rule is stated three inconsistent ways (lower-bound rule in the body, trichotomy in Figure 3, upper-bound certification evidence in the caption). 3) Theory-quality gaps: Thm 4.7(iii)'s appendix derivation has both inequality directions flipped (statement right, proof corrupt); Thm 4.8's sketch attributes a normal-approximation concentration to Hoeffding (false at the stated operating point); Prop 4.4's sketch does not establish the claimed probe count; Corollary 4.9 has no proof and overreaches ('against any detection budget'); beta_d serves triple duty (false-alarm rate, detection cap, power complement); z_beta_d is defined only in the appendix; and the patch-decay law (RQ3's flagship) is never invoked after Section 4. 4) Evidence denominators a referee cannot reconstruct: E1's 1,500 episodes vs 75 cells x 60; E27's '60 sessions' with n=30 Wilson intervals; E3/E23's per-cell batch sizes; the 1,230-session audit corpus membership; the 118-flag per-panel decomposition; E31's registration date (2026-11-23) vs Table 5's caption ('2026-11-22/23'). 5) Craft: a 340-word abstract with a 62-word path sentence and undefined 'frontier-catalog'; a ~200-word conclusion sentence; the E21 paragraph's triple-nested 130-word caveat; 'Nothing changes between foil and field' and 'the instrument measures what it claims to measure' are the two uncalibrated universals in an otherwise calibrated paper. 6) Presentation drift: cross-reference types wrong twice ('Propositions 7.3-7.8' spans Theorem 7.4 and Corollary 7.5; 'Theorems 7.4 and 7.5'), '8.1M SSH sessions' misquoting an interactions count, 'most-cited survey' unsupported, 'Treason Bricken' and a stray accent macro in the bibliography; five of six included figures lack the accessibility Description; x-axis of Fig 5(b) hides the stated anchors. 7) Boundary claims: 'no model... complies' is five tested models, not a universal; 'released for the field to replicate' overstates what withheld probe sets permit; '30 pre-registered' flattens the 25/5 confirmatory/post-anomaly split the paper's own rigor section insists on.

questions.text: 1) Give the E1 grid definition (cells x n per cell) that makes the 1,500-episode count exact, and per-family dose-response correlations with dispersion. 2) Which family in the graded foil is designed at beta=1? E14's 0.067 advantage is unrecomputable without it. 3) What is the E27 denominator: 30 sessions per model (then say so) or 60 pooled? 4) What are the six runs in the 1,230-session leakage-audit corpus? 5) Does E30-MiniMax contribute flags to the 118/112 totals (its Table 5 row is 'unmeasurable')? 6) Exact registration vs data-start timestamps for E31 vs Table 5's '2026-11-22/23'. 7) Were the 50 constructed boundary-audit labels assigned blind to oracle outputs? 8) What attacker capability generates E15's intermediate 0.100 point? 9) Define E20's defender utility and its Laplace-epsilon grid. 10) Why 301 fresh target processes for 300 session ids? 11) Which infelicities are typesetting vs conversion: the spaced-decimal macros break text extraction of every number in the PDF - is that deliberate?
